signals.name: Barclays' H2 2026 survey ($8.7T AUM) names market-neutral and macro the two most in-demand strategies
signals.reading: Barclays surveyed 340 investors representing $8.7T in AUM: 43% expect to be net allocators to hedge funds in H2 2026 (the strongest backdrop in years); Equity Market Neutral is the most sought-after strategy (29% investor interest), Global Macro second (27%), Quant Multi-Strategy third (23%) and Equity Statistical Arbitrage fourth (19%). Separately, Goldman Sachs' own 2026 outlook found almost half of allocators plan to increase hedge fund allocations this year, with quant and macro cited as the most favored categories
signals.level: Market Neutral #1 (29%), Global Macro #2 (27%) investor interest; 43% net allocators, $8.7T surveyed AUM
signals.angle: Third-party validation, now from two separate large surveys (Barclays and Goldman), that CCM8752's two lead sleeves (Picton market-neutral, iAGAM macro) sit in exactly the categories institutional allocators say they want most right now — a strong, current answer to 'why alternatives, why these strategies, why now'

ELITE.compositionNote: Elite Pools & Unified Portfolios continue to draw on PIMCO, Loomis Sayles and iAGAM as sub-advisors. The one confirmed structural change this year remains at iAGAM itself: the Asset Allocation team that steers strategic/tactical tilts across these pools is now led by Tej Rai and Alex Bellefleur following Sébastien Mc Mahon's move to Chief Economist, iA Financial Group (May 19/26) — with a second source today corroborating that the same handover extends to 4 segregated funds effective Sep 14/26. On the PIMCO side, Bloomberg's Sep 4/26 report now has a name and detail attached: manager Emmanuel Sharef's ~$19B fund (outperforming 97% of peers over 3 years) is rotating out of 'Magnificent Seven' US tech and into Asian AI-supply-chain names — semiconductor, memory, optical, cooling, power and construction-equipment suppliers, plus rare earths and industrial metals. Loomis Sayles has not published anything reacting to the latest oil/equity moves; its most recent dated outlook (Aug/26) called for the Fed to hold through year-end, which now reads as potentially stale given the more hawkish repricing under Fed Chair Warsh and this week's volatile hike-odds swings (see CCM5604). iA Clarington's overall AUM (>$26B, Jul 31/26) and iAGAM's firm-wide AUM ($156B, Jun 30/26) were both reconfirmed. This week's live macro test for the fixed-income sub-advisors inside these pools has only sharpened: oil is holding above $100/barrel, US equities have fallen three straight sessions, and the Canada-US tariff war has a new flashpoint in Trump's threatened Bombardier import ban.
